title: Jack Carey and Tiger Rag
summary: Allen asks about unrecorded clarinetists, then Hall explains Jack Carey's fame for Tiger Rag, nicknamed for it.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Did you ever know Blond Freddy, a clarinet player by that name? Blond Freddy, no. Did you ever know Isidore Fritz, who's from out in the country somewhere? Isidore Fritz, huh? I just wondered how those fellas played, and we don't have any records of them. Blond Freddy's still alive, but he doesn't play clarinet. No, no, I don't know them. Who does Jack Carey play like on one of the other ones?

Play like Jack Carey, I guess. They used to call him, by you know they changed his name, they used to call him Tiger Rag. And all they changed, they tuned Tiger Rag to Jack Carey. When they wanted Tiger Rag, they said, play Jack Carey, and he used to do some kind of triple tug in that Tiger Rag, and everybody used to go for that.
There's nobody around today that you think compares with him?
With who? With Jack Carey's style.
With, you know, with Jack Carey. Did O'Replay it all like him?
Well, yeah, on that same order, but Jack Carey was noted for that Tiger Rag. Tiger Rag, that was his famous tune. He made his name through that, playing that Tiger Rag.
